title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 44–46): over a base S with residue characteristics ≠ 2, Grothendieck classifies faithful actions of the Klein four-group V ≅ (Z/2)^2 on a P^1-bundle X/S. Each involution σ_i of V is determined by its fixed-point divisor Δ_i = X^{σ_i}, an étale divisor of degree 2 (an 'axis'). The goal is a local normal form, from which he defines the 'configuration octaédrale' Δ = Δ1 ⊔ Δ2 ⊔ Δ3, an étale divisor of degree 6. This feeds his study of moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.

This page proves the local normal form.

(i) Normalising σ1. The pair (X, Δ1) is unique up to local isomorphism. After an étale-local trivialisation of Δ1, one has (X, Δ1) ≅ (P^1_S, {0, ∞}). The involution with fixed points 0 and ∞ is z ↦ −z. Then X∖Δ1 = G_{m,S}, and the quotient by {1, σ1} is again G_{m,S}, with quotient map λ ↦ λ^2.

(ii) Choosing σ2. By the previous page, σ2 (equivalently Δ2) corresponds to a section of (X∖Δ1)/⟨σ1⟩, i.e. a unit λ on S. Since 2 is invertible, étale-locally λ = ξ^2 with ξ a section of X∖Δ1 (Kummer theory). Then Δ2 = {ξ, −ξ}.

(iii) Rescaling. Replace the coordinate z by z/ξ to get ξ = 1. This gives the standard situation (4): Δ1 = {0, ∞}, Δ2 = {1, −1}, σ1(z) = −z, σ2(z) = 1/z. Here σ2 is the unique homography exchanging 0 and ∞ and fixing ±1.

(iv) Next page. It follows that σ3(z) = −1/z and Δ3 = V(z^2 + 1), i.e. {±i} when a primitive 4th root of unity exists. So étale-locally every faithful V-action is the standard Klein-four action on P^1. The six points {0, ∞, ±1, ±i} are the vertices of the octahedron.
errors: No mathematical errors. Implicit points are all correct but left unstated: the involution with a given fixed étale divisor of degree 2 is unique (char ≠ 2); commutation forces σ2 to swap 0 and ∞, since otherwise it would have 4 fixed points; and Δ2 = {ξ, −ξ} is étale because 2 and ξ are invertible.
The phrase 'l'homomorphisme de passage au quotient' refers to a morphism of schemes (λ ↦ λ^2 is also a group homomorphism of G_m, so this is harmless).

ideas.what: Étale-local normal form of a faithful Klein four-group action on a P^1-bundle over a base with 2 invertible: σ1 = −z, σ2 = 1/z, σ3 = −1/z
ideas.modern_name: Klein four subgroup of PGL_2 / dihedral D_2 ⊂ PGL_2; étale-local triviality of V-actions on Brauer–Severi curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, finite subgroups of PGL_2); the scheme-theoretic version is folklore

ideas.what: Section of the quotient (X∖Δ1)/σ1 ≅ G_m lifted étale-locally via Kummer extraction of a square root
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory / μ_2-torsor G_m → G_m, λ ↦ λ^2

ideas.what: Octahedral configuration {0, ∞, ±1, ±i} as the union of the three axes of a V-action (defined on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral configuration; vertices of the octahedron, related to the cusps of X(4) and to level-2 structures

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine relative (over-a-base) version of the classical normal form for the Klein four-group acting on P^1. Nothing on the page would surprise a specialist. Any interest would lie in how the octahedral configuration is later used for elliptic-curve moduli, which is not on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'la situation st. est' should be read as 'la situation standard est'.
'La donnée d'une section ... équivaut donc : celle d'une section' should read 'équivaut donc à celle d'une section λ de G_{mS}'.
'loc. pour la top. étale, on peut poser λ = ξ^2, i.e. [λ] provenant d'une section ξ de X∖Δ1 sur S' (with the crossed-out text omitted) is correct.
'45' at bottom left is the archive page number.
On the next page, 'racine primitive de ξ−1 [?]' is more plausibly 'racine primitive 4-ième de 1' (a primitive fourth root of unity), consistent with {i, −i}.
On the next page, 'D_4 = F_2 × F_2' is likely 'D_2' or V, i.e. the Klein four-group.
